t: Immediate Food Delivery III — Conditional Aggregation
o: An order is immediate when order_date equals customer_pref_delivery_date. Group rows by order_date and report the percentage of immediate orders, rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by date. In the sample, 2019-08-01 has 2 of 3 immediate → 66.67. This is a straight GROUP BY with a boolean-average (MySQL) or conditional aggregation (standard SQL).
k: order_date = customer_pref_delivery_date is a boolean expression; averaging it yields the fraction immediate in MySQL.

a.i: In MySQL, TRUE is 1 and FALSE is 0, so AVG(order_date = customer_pref_delivery_date) * 100 is exactly the immediate percentage per group.

c.python:
-- SQL solution (same statement for all engines below)
SELECT order_date,
       ROUND(AVG(order_date = customer_pref_delivery_date) * 100, 2) AS immediate_percentage
FROM Delivery
GROUP BY order_date
ORDER BY order_date;

a.t: O(R log R) — grouping/sorting the R rows of Delivery.
a.sp: O(G) — one output row per distinct order_date.

a.i: Standard SQL has no boolean-to-int average, so use SUM(CASE WHEN ...) / COUNT(*) — portable across PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, etc. Multiply by 100.0 to force decimal division.
s: immediate_percentage = ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_date = customer_pref_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2).

c.python:
SELECT order_date,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_date = customer_pref_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS immediate_percentage
FROM Delivery
GROUP BY order_date
ORDER BY order_date;

w: Prefer the CASE WHEN form for portability; the AVG(boolean) trick is a nice MySQL idiom to mention. Pitfalls: integer division truncating the ratio (use 100.0), forgetting ROUND to exactly 2 places, and missing the final ORDER BY. Follow-up: overall immediate percentage across all dates (single-row variant), or per-customer percentages.
